findings.span: Comfyで働く理由
findings.suggestion: …で働く理由
findings.reason: This is the 'before' fragment of a split heading; the brand name is normally supplied by the adjacent highlighted segment. Inserting 'Comfy' here risks rendering the brand twice in the assembled heading.

findings.span: 少数精鋭です
findings.suggestion: 少人数で、熱量の高いチームです
findings.reason: "少数精鋭" (small and elite) adds a claim of eliteness the English does not make and drops "intense".

findings.span: 創作のための新しいエコシステムを生み出しました
findings.suggestion: 創作のための新しく強力なエコシステムを生み出しました
findings.reason: Omits "powerful" from a direct attributed quotation; quoted material should not drop qualifiers.

findings.span: オープンソースプロジェクトから生まれ、ビジュアル
findings.suggestion: ビジュアル
findings.reason: The concatenated heading becomes "...となったAIツール" (an AI tool), introducing a subject noun the English never uses; the English subject is the open-source project itself. Also the split shifts "AI" into the highlighted fragment, so the emphasised text will read "AIのプロフェッショナル標準" instead of just "professional standard".

findings.span: 投資家
findings.suggestion: 私たちの投資家
findings.reason: Sibling section labels in the same page render 'OUR ...' as 私たちの歩み / 私たちの価値観, but this one drops the possessive, making the label set inconsistent.

findings.span: 世に出すもののために努力する。
findings.suggestion: 世に出すもののために努力します。
findings.reason: Style mix inside one body string: the first sentence is plain form while the second uses です・ます, and all other card bodies are consistently polite.

findings.span: クラフトを尊重する
findings.suggestion: 技を尊重する
findings.reason: Katakana クラフト in Japanese normally suggests handicraft/craft goods, not craftsmanship or skill; a native reader would expect 技 or 職人技 here.

findings.span: こんな方を求めています…
findings.suggestion: こんな方なら…
findings.reason: The English "If you are..." is a conditional lead-in that flows into the list below. Rendering it as "we are looking for people like this" duplicates the heading directly above it (募集している方) and breaks the sentence continuation into the list items.

findings.span: 幅広いクリエイティブコントロール
findings.suggestion: 完全なクリエイティブコントロール
findings.reason: English says 'full creative control'; the translation weakens it to 'wide-ranging control', which is a different claim.

findings.span: よりも幅広いクリエイティブコントロールが可能
findings.suggestion: …クリエイティブコントロールが可能です
findings.reason: Style inconsistency within the same benefit list: the sibling sentence-form descriptions use です・ます endings while this full sentence ends in a bare noun form.

findings.span: 新しいタブで開きました。—
findings.suggestion: 新しいタブで開きました —
findings.reason: Doubled punctuation: a Japanese full stop immediately followed by an em dash. The dash is a connector to the following link fragment ('open them here'), so the sentence-ending 。 should be dropped for the concatenated sentence to read naturally.

findings.span: スタック全体にComfyUIを統合
findings.suggestion: 既存のスタックにComfyUIを統合
findings.reason: English says 'the rest of your stack' (the surrounding/existing stack), while the translation says 'the entire stack', and the possessive 'your' is dropped.

findings.span: ミーティングの予約が完了しました。カレンダー招待と会議リンクはメールでご確認ください。
findings.suggestion: ミーティングの予約が完了しました。カレンダー招待とミーティングリンクはメールでご確認ください。
findings.reason: The English word 'meeting' is rendered two ways within the same sentence (ミーティング for the booking, 会議 for the link). Pick one rendering for consistency across this page (bookingConfirmation.checkEmail uses 会議リンク as well).

findings.span: 商標ガイドライン
findings.suggestion: 商標ガイドライン。
findings.reason: Sentence-final punctuation is inconsistent with the other headings in the same page (brand.colors.heading and brand.logos.heading both keep the full stop from the English), so headings read as stylistically mismatched.

findings.span: 直接的
findings.suggestion: 率直
findings.reason: For a brand-voice trait, 直接的 reads as a literal dictionary rendering; 率直 is the natural Japanese label for a 'direct' tone of voice.

findings.span: Comfy Cloudノード
findings.suggestion: Comfy Cloud ノード
findings.reason: Missing space between the Latin-script product name and the following katakana word; Japanese typography normally inserts a space here for readability.

findings.span: フォワードデプロイメント・クリエイティブテクノロジスト
findings.suggestion: フォワードデプロイド・クリエイティブテクノロジスト
findings.reason: The English is 'Forward Deployed' (past participle, describing the technologist). The transliteration renders it as 'Forward Deployment' (a noun), slightly altering the job title.

findings.span: 支えるオープンソースコミュニティを深く大切にしています
findings.suggestion: 私たちが支えるオープンソースコミュニティを深く大切にしています
findings.reason: The relative clause has no explicit subject, so '支える' can be misread as the community supporting us rather than 'the open-source community we serve'. Adding 私たちが removes the ambiguity.

findings.span: オープンでモジュール型の世界をリードするビジュアルAIプラットフォーム
findings.suggestion: 世界をリードする、オープンでモジュール型のビジュアルAIプラットフォーム
findings.reason: Stacked modifiers make it read momentarily as 'an open, modular world' before 'leading platform'; reordering makes the noun phrase parse cleanly.

findings.span: 基盤技術に携わりたい
findings.suggestion: すでに実際の動画、画像、音楽、アプリを支えている基盤技術に取り組むのが好き。
findings.reason: English says 'Like working on' (a preference/enjoyment); the translation renders it as 'want to work on' (desire), duplicating the phrasing of reason1 and slightly shifting meaning.

findings.span: Comfy MCPは、チャットで対話的にエージェント作業を行うためのもので
findings.suggestion: Comfy MCP は、チャットで対話的にエージェント作業を行うためのもので
findings.reason: Orthographic inconsistency across the same page: the cli.agents strings insert a space between Latin/Latin-flag tokens and Japanese text (e.g. '--json を受け付け', 'CLI 自体'), while the cli.faq answers omit it ('CLIは', 'Comfy MCPは', '--downloadで'). Spacing should be uniform throughout the section.

findings.span: 既存の[Comfy Cloud subscription](https://comfy.org/cloud/pricing)
findings.suggestion: 既存の[Comfy Cloud サブスクリプション](https://comfy.org/cloud/pricing)
findings.reason: The link label was left partly untranslated: 'subscription' is a common noun (not a protected proper noun) and reads as an untranslated fragment inside a Japanese sentence. Only 'Comfy Cloud' must stay English.

findings.span: すべてのシェル
findings.suggestion: 任意のシェル
findings.reason: 'Any shell' means 'whichever shell you use', not 'all shells'. Also inconsistent with cli.meta.description, which renders the same phrase as 任意のシェル.

findings.span: 検索
findings.suggestion: 見つける / 探索
findings.reason: Step heading 'DISCOVER' is rendered as '検索' (search), narrowing the step name; the search action is already covered in the body copy below it.

findings.span: comfy jobs waitで完了を待機し
findings.suggestion: comfy jobs waitで進行状況を追跡し
findings.reason: English says the command 'tracks it'; the translation says it waits for completion, which narrows the stated behaviour.

findings.span: GPUは不要です。ジョブはComfy CloudのGPUで実行されます。
findings.suggestion: GPU は不要です。ジョブは Comfy Cloud の GPU で実行されます。
findings.reason: Latin/Japanese spacing is inconsistent within the same section: several strings (e.g. cli.session.subtitle, cli.setup.agent.description) insert spaces around Latin terms while this and other setup strings do not. Unify the convention.

findings.span: ./characters. 内の
findings.suggestion: ./characters 内の各ヒーローの4面ターンアラウンドを生成。
findings.reason: The English sentence-final period was absorbed into the file path, producing a malformed path ('./characters.') followed by a stray space. The path should read './characters' and the sentence should end with the period/。 after the verb.

findings.span: 渡して。
findings.suggestion: Align register with the sibling prompt card (e.g. noun/plain form such as 「…を作成し、.glb を出力。」)
findings.reason: Sibling skill-card prompt (characterSheets) ends in a noun-style '生成。' while this one uses a casual spoken imperative '渡して。'; the two cards are read side by side and should share one register.

findings.span: ./shots.にダウンロードして
findings.suggestion: ./shots にダウンロードして
findings.reason: A period was appended directly to the file path, turning './shots' into './shots.' and corrupting a copy-pasteable path. Separate the path from the sentence punctuation.

findings.span: Comfy CLIを選ぶ？
findings.suggestion: Comfy CLIなのか？
findings.reason: Combined heading reads "なぜComfy CLIを選ぶ？" — a plain-form verb directly followed by a question mark is unidiomatic for a Japanese heading; the nominalised form (なのか / を選ぶのか) is the standard pattern.

findings.span: 任意のホステッドサービス
findings.suggestion: オプションのホスト型サービス
findings.reason: '任意の' here reads as 'arbitrary/any' rather than 'optional', and it repeats the 任意の used earlier in the same string for 'however you want'; unnatural phrasing for 'optional hosted service'.

findings.span: 料金に関するFAQ
findings.suggestion: 料金に関するよくある質問
findings.reason: The same link label 'Pricing FAQs' is rendered as 料金に関するFAQ here but 料金に関するよくある質問 in cloud.faq.footer, and the section heading uses よくある質問; inconsistent on one page.

findings.span: どのコンピューターを使っていても、ブラウザからすぐに作成を始められます。
findings.suggestion: いいえ。どのコンピューターを使っていても、ブラウザからすぐに作成を始められます。
findings.reason: The initial 'No' answering the yes/no question is dropped, while other answers in the same FAQ set do render 'Yes' as はい; inconsistent and slightly less clear.

findings.span: 独自にファインチューニングしたLoRAを持ち込み、独自のスタイルを仕上げられます
findings.suggestion: ファインチューニング済みのLoRAを持ち込み、自分だけのスタイルを追求できます
findings.reason: '独自' is repeated twice in one clause, which reads clumsy in Japanese; vary the wording.

findings.span: 限定
findings.suggestion: ONLY ON badge should be phrased so it reads correctly before the CLOUD badge, e.g. "こちらだけ" / or move 限定 into the CLOUD badge ("クラウド限定")
findings.reason: This badge is displayed together with cloud.reason.2.badge.cloud ("クラウド"), producing "限定 クラウド". Japanese word order requires the qualifier after the noun ("クラウド限定"), so the two badges read backwards as rendered.

findings.span: 選ぶ理由
findings.suggestion: プロフェッショナルが\n選ぶのは\n
findings.reason: The English heading is an incomplete sentence ending in 'choose ' because the product name is appended after it by the layout. The Japanese ends with the noun '理由' ('the reason'), so the appended product name will follow the completed phrase and produce broken word order (e.g. 'プロフェッショナルが選ぶ理由 Comfy Cloud'). The fragment needs to end in a form that a following product name can complete.

findings.span: GitHub スター
findings.suggestion: GitHub スター数
findings.reason: Inconsistent with the sibling metric label 'ダウンロード数' (cloudNodes.detail.downloads); Japanese UI normally appends 数 for count metrics shown side by side.

findings.span: Comfy Cloud のマネージド GPU ですぐに実行できます
findings.suggestion: Comfy Cloud にプリインストール済みで、マネージド GPU ですぐに実行できます
findings.reason: The English 'preinstalled on Comfy Cloud' is dropped; only 'ready to run' survives. Other strings on this page (metaDescription) do render it as プリインストール済み, so the hero loses a selling point stated in the source.

findings.span: 音声用に
findings.suggestion: オーディオ用に
findings.reason: '音声' in Japanese tech copy usually means voice/speech, whereas the English 'for audio' refers to music generation (MiniMax Music 3). 'オーディオ' is the more accurate rendering.

findings.span: 他のノードと同様に接続して実行します。
findings.suggestion: 他のノードと同様に接続するだけです。
findings.reason: The English sentence only says to wire the node like any other node; the translation adds 'and run' (実行します), which is not stated in this sentence (it duplicates the step label).

findings.span: SOC 2 Type II監査を進行中です。
findings.suggestion: SOC 2 Type II 監査を進行中です。
findings.reason: Inconsistent orthography within the same page: a1-a3 insert a space between Latin script and Japanese (e.g. 'MiniMax 商用利用ライセンス', 'Comfy Enterprise を見る'), while a4 and the question strings omit it ('SOC 2 Type II監査', 'MiniMaxの商用ライセンス'). Should be uniform.

findings.span: ワークフローを構築し、
findings.suggestion: 強力なワークフローを構築し、
findings.reason: The English heading's qualifier 'powerful' in 'Create powerful workflows' is dropped, weakening the claim the source does make. Minor omission.

findings.span: 詳しくない私でも
findings.suggestion: 詳しくない人でも
findings.reason: The English says 'even for someone who isn't familiar with it all' — a generic third person, not the reviewer. The translation converts it to first person ('even I, who am not familiar'), a small unsupported shift.

findings.span: 新たなエコシステムを築きました
findings.suggestion: 新たで強力なエコシステムを生み出しました
findings.reason: Omits 'powerful' from 'a new and powerful ecosystem'; the qualifier is present in the English source and is dropped in the translation.

findings.span: 当社のクリエイティブパイプラインに欠かせません
findings.suggestion: 当社のクリエイティブパイプラインを大きく変えました
findings.reason: "is a game changer for our creative pipeline" is rendered as "is indispensable to our creative pipeline", which states something different (indispensability rather than transformative change) in a direct customer quote.

findings.span: ノードベースのワークフローにより、プロセスの各ステップを完全に管理しながら、迅速に試行できます。
findings.suggestion: ノードベースのワークフローにより、プロセスの各ステップを完全に管理しながら、柔軟かつ迅速に試行できます。
findings.reason: "gives us the flexibility to experiment rapidly" — the notion of flexibility is omitted from the translation.

findings.span: 革新的でクリエイティブな企業
findings.suggestion: 最も革新的でクリエイティブな企業
findings.reason: The English superlative 'the most innovative and creative' is flattened to a plain adjective; the intensifier is omitted.

findings.span: 「開始」アクション
findings.suggestion: 「Get Started」アクション

findings.span: コミュニティワークフローハブ
findings.suggestion: コミュニティ Workflow Hub
findings.reason: The feature name is rendered as Latin-script "Hub" in the page title (demos.community-workflows.title) but as katakana "ハブ" in the body, so the same product surface is named two different ways in strings shown together.

findings.span: 次のデモ
findings.suggestion: 次のステップ
findings.reason: English label is the generic "What's Next"; the translation narrows it to "next demo", stating something more specific than the source.

findings.span: 活用して
findings.suggestion: 見てみましょう / 探してみましょう
findings.reason: English says "Explore" (browse/discover), but the translation says "make use of", shifting the intended action; also inconsistent with the title's 探す.

findings.span: クリックしてテンプレートを読み込み、パラメータを調整します。
findings.suggestion: クリックしてテンプレートを読み込み、必要に応じてパラメータを調整します。

findings.span: プロフェッショナルが\n選ぶ理由\n
findings.suggestion: …をプロフェッショナルが選ぶ理由 (place the appended product name before the Japanese text, e.g. by restructuring the fragment so the concatenated name reads naturally)
findings.reason: The English ends with a trailing space, indicating a product name is concatenated after this heading fragment ('Why professionals choose <Product>'). The Japanese ends with 理由 ('the reason'), so the appended product name would dangle after the completed sentence, producing an ungrammatical heading. findings.span: Comfy エンタープライズ

findings.suggestion: 私のようなアーティストは、何も自動化したくありません。
findings.reason: Subject/predicate mismatch: the topic marker 「〜にとって」 does not agree with the volitional predicate 「したいとは思いません」, which reads awkwardly. A native writer would use 「私のようなアーティストは…したくありません」.

findings.span: IP-AdapterとControlNetで駆動するStable Diffusion 1.5でのスタイル転写
findings.suggestion: IP-AdapterとControlNetで駆動されるStable Diffusion 1.5でのスタイル転写
findings.reason: Active 「駆動する」 makes Stable Diffusion the driver rather than the thing being driven; the English has it driven BY IP-Adapter and ControlNet, so the passive form is needed.

findings.span: カスタムLoRAsも学習させました
findings.suggestion: カスタムLoRAも学習させました
findings.reason: Japanese does not take the English plural -s on loanwords; the approved term form is 'LoRA'. Same issue recurs in the At a glance table.

findings.span: 自身で撮影した都市映像で学習したカスタムLoRAs
findings.suggestion: 自身で撮影した都市映像で学習したカスタムLoRA
findings.reason: English plural '-s' retained on the term LoRA; Japanese should use the singular Latin-script form 'LoRA'.

findings.span: 複雑なコンポジット
findings.suggestion: 大量のコンポジット作業
findings.reason: 'heavy compositing' refers to the amount/intensity of compositing work, not its complexity; 複雑な states something the English does not claim.

findings.span: 私のアートを奪うのはツールではありません。私のアートを広げるツールです。
findings.suggestion: ツールは私のアートを奪うものではなく、広げてくれるものです。
findings.reason: The second sentence has no subject and reads as a fragment in Japanese; merging the contrast into one sentence reads more naturally as a pull quote.

findings.span: Golden Awardを受賞し
findings.suggestion: 金賞を受賞し
findings.reason: The same prize is called 金賞 in the heading but left as 'Golden Award' in the body of the same section; use one form consistently.

findings.span: WAN 3.0を実行
findings.suggestion: Wan 3.0を実行
findings.reason: Product name must appear exactly as 'Wan 3.0'; the all-caps 'WAN 3.0' comes from the English button styling and is not a Japanese typographic convention, and it also mismatches 'Wan 3.0' used in every other string on this page.

findings.span: Wan 3.0 は Wan 2.7 から何が新しくなりましたか？
findings.suggestion: Wan 3.0はWan 2.7から何が新しくなりましたか？
findings.reason: Inconsistent spacing: this string inserts ASCII spaces around the Japanese particles/product names, while the sibling FAQ strings in the same block (e.g. 'Wan 3.0へのプロンプト', 'Wan 3.0で手持ちの動画') use no spaces. Should match the rest of the section.

findings.span: WAN ANIMATE 2 を実行
findings.suggestion: Wan Animate 2 を実行
findings.reason: Product name is set in all caps, altering the required exact form of the proper noun, and it is inconsistent with wanAnimate2.hero.primaryCta on the same page, which uses 'Wan Animate 2を実行'.

findings.span: ドライビング動画
findings.suggestion: 動きの元となる動画
findings.reason: 'Driving video' is rendered as a transliteration here but as '動きの元となる動画' in wanAnimate2.meta.description on the same page; the two should match.

findings.span: 転送したい動き
findings.suggestion: 適用したい動き
findings.reason: 転送 means data forwarding/transmission in Japanese and reads oddly for motion transfer; other strings on the page use 適用 for the same concept.

findings.span: ショットを書く
findings.suggestion: ショットを記述
findings.reason: Heading style is inconsistent with the sibling step title '参照素材をアップロード', which uses a noun/stem ending as Japanese UI headings do; this one uses a plain dictionary-form verb sentence.

findings.span: 最適なAIモデルで構築
findings.suggestion: 最高のAIモデルで構築
findings.reason: '最適な' means 'most suitable/optimal', shifting the meaning of 'the best' toward 'the right one for you'. '最高の' matches the English claim more directly.
